questions.question: Who was the designer of India’s national flag?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Pingali Venkayya.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pingali Venkayya **was an Indian freedom fighter and the designer of the Indian national flag.
 
• The final version of flag was adopted on July 22, 1947,
 
• Venkayya earned the **nickname "Japan Venkayya" **because of his expertise in the Japanese language.
 
• The colors of flag were also interpreted to represent broader ideals: **saffron for courage and sacrifice, white for peace and truth, and green for faith and chivalry.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **B.N. Rau, (Benegal Narsing Rau), **was civil servant, jurist, and diplomat in India during the mid-20th century.
 
• B.N. Rau was **Constitutional Advisor **to the Constituent Assembly of India. He was responsible **for preparing the initial draft of the Indian Constitution. **
 
• He passed away on November 30, 1953, while serving on the **International Court of Justice.**
 
• **Prem Behari Narain Raizada **was a notable figure for his distinctive role in the creation of the **handwritten final copy of the Constitution of India**.
 
• Prem Behari Narain Raizada's contribution was to produce **the final, official document of the Indian Constitution**. 
 
• Raizada **refused to charge any fee **for his work.
 
• **Kanhaiyalal Maneklal Munshi, (K.M. Munshi), **was a distinguished Indian independence activist, politician, writer, and educationist.
 
• He was involved in several key events, including the **Salt Satyagraha and the Quit India Movement.**
 
• 
 
K.M. Munshi was also a prolific writer. Some of his notable works include: **Pattani Prabhuta, Gujarat and its literature and Jay Somanth.**

questions.question: In 2023, Government of India has proposed to launch the ‘Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana’ ___________ to skill lakhs of youth within the next three years covering new age courses like coding, AI, robotics, mechatronics, IOT, 3D printing, drones and soft skills.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.0.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2023, the Government of India launched ‘Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana** 4.0** (PMKVY 4.0)’, as part of its continued effort to upskill India's youth in emerging technologies.
 
• The aim is to train over** 4.2 lakh youth **over the next three years, covering modern areas like artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, coding, drones, 3D printing, mechatronics, Internet of Things (IoT), and soft skills.
 
• The scheme also focuses on industry-based learning to ensure that participants acquire skills that align with market demands.
 
• The **key objectives** include:
 
 
• Enhancing employability by providing vocational training and certification in new-age technologies.
 
• Incorporating international standards into the curriculum for globally recognized certifications.
 
• Promoting self-employment and entrepreneurship alongside providing placements in relevant industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) has been implemented in phases since its inception, each aiming to build on the last in terms of training India’s workforce for new and emerging industries.

 
• **PMKVY 1.0 (2015-2016):**

 
 
• Launch Date: 15 July **2015**
 
• Goal: To provide skill training to around 24 lakh youth across the country in various sectors.
 
• Focused on short-term training programs through training centers accredited by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).
 
• Outcome: More than 19 lakh candidates were trained, but the placement rate was a key challenge, as the training did not always align with industry demand.
 
 
 
• **PMKVY 2.0 (2016-2020):**
 
 
• Launch Date: 2 October **2016**
 
• Goal: Upskilling of over 1 crore people by 2020.
 
• Expanded to cover more sectors and introduced Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) for workers who already possess certain skills.
 
• Focus on placements with the introduction of mandatory placement tracking and support.
 
• Increased participation of state governments in the scheme for local adaptability.
 
• Special Projects were introduced to cater to the specific needs of certain industries, job roles, or regions.
 
• Outcome: It significantly increased reach but faced criticism for not achieving a high placement rate despite the broader scope.
 
 
 
• **PMKVY 3.0 (2020-2021):**
 
• Launch Date: January 15, **2021**
 
 
• Goal: To skill over 8 lakh people in emerging areas over one year.
 
• Shifted focus towards local demand-based skill training.
 
• Emphasized digital learning to adapt to the post-pandemic world, incorporating online and blended training modes.
 
• Introduction of district skill committees to identify demand-driven skills specific to local areas.
 
• Strengthened the focus on apprenticeship training and linking skilling with employment.
 
• Outcome: PMKVY 3.0 aimed to refine earlier challenges by localizing skill development and incorporating emerging technologies like AI, cybersecurity, and cloud computing.
 
 

Each version of the PMKVY scheme aimed to improve India’s skill ecosystem by adapting to the evolving needs of the labor market and technological advancements. PMKVY 4.0 continues this effort by focusing on futuristic technologies and aligning the training program with global standards.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 20(2).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 20(2) specifically states: "No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once."
 
• This provision protects individuals from being tried again for an offense after a judgment has already been rendered, whether the judgment is acquittal or conviction.
 
• It is part of the **fundamental rights **guaranteed by the Constitution and is aimed at protecting individuals from double jeopardy.
 
• The term "**double jeopardy**" refers to the legal principle that a person cannot be tried or punished for the same offense more than once.
 
• This principle is rooted in the notion of fairness and justice, ensuring that individuals are not subjected to repeated legal proceedings for the same act.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Fundamental Right
 Article
 Description
 Key Features
 
 
 
 

 Right to Equality
 Article 14
 Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws for all individuals.
 Prohibits discrimination based on religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
 

 Right to Freedom
 Articles 19-22
 Provides various freedoms, including speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 Includes the right to life and personal liberty. Restrictions can be imposed for public order, morality, etc.
 
 

 Right Against Exploitation
 Articles 23-24
 Prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and child labor.
 Ensures protection from exploitation and forced labor.
 
 

 Right to Freedom of Religion
 Articles 25-28
 Guarantees the freedom of conscience and the right to profess, practice, and propagate any religion.
 Ensures equality of all religions and allows religious practices.
 
 

 Cultural and Educational Rights
 Articles 29-30
 Protects the rights of minorities to conserve their culture, language, and script, and to establish educational institutions.
 Ensures the right of minorities to preserve their identity and cultural heritage.
 
 

 Right to Constitutional Remedies
 Article 32
 Provides the right to approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 Allows individuals to seek enforcement of rights through writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari.
 
 

 Right to Privacy
 Article 21
 Although not explicitly mentioned, the Supreme Court has recognized the right to privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21.
 Protects personal autonomy and privacy in various aspects of life.

questions.question: The transfer of heat through horizontal movement of air is called _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Advection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Advection refers to the transfer of heat or other atmospheric properties (such as moisture) through the **horizontal movement of air masses.**
 
• **Warm air advection (WAA):** Occurs when warmer air is transported into a region, leading to rising temperatures.
 
• **Cold air advection (CAA): **Occurs when colder air is transported into a region, often resulting in a drop in temperature.
 
• Advection is responsible for redistributing heat from one region to another, helping to **balance temperature differences across the globe.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Property**
 **Conduction**
 **Convection**
 **Radiation**
 
 

 Transfer Mechanism
 Direct contact, molecular collisions
 Movement of fluids due to temperature/density
 Electromagnetic waves
 
 

 Occurs In
 Solids (mostly), also in liquids and gases
 Liquids and gases
 Across empty space or through any medium
 
 

 Examples
 Metal spoon heating in hot soup
 Boiling water, sea breezes
 Sun's heat reaches Earth, feeling the warmth from the fire.
 
 

 Medium Required
 Yes (solid, liquid, or gas)
 Yes (fluid: liquid or gas)
 No (can transfer through a vacuum).

questions.question: _____ is the science and art of cultivating fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Horticulture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Horticulture is derived from the **Latin words “hortus” (garden) and “cultura” (cultivation)**, meaning garden cultivation.
 
• It covers multiple categories, including **pomology, olericulture, floriculture, landscape horticulture, and post-harvest management**.
 
• Horticulture includes** organic farming, integrated pest management (IPM),** and the use of natural resources efficiently.
 
• **Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)** is a government initiative to promote horticultural development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Major Divisions of Horticulture**:

 
 
• **Pomology**: The science of fruit and nut cultivation (e.g., apples, oranges, mangoes).
 
• **Olericulture**: The science of growing vegetables (e.g., tomatoes, carrots, spinach).
 
• **Floriculture**: The cultivation of flowering and ornamental plants for gardens, floral industry, and landscape design.
 
• **Viticulture**: The cultivation of grapes (used for making wine, raisins, and juice).
 
• **Arboriculture**: The care and management of trees, including shade trees and ornamental tree.
 
 
 
• **Floriculture** is the cultivation and management of **flowering** and ornamental plants for gardens, floral industry, and decorative purposes.
 
• **Viniculture** (also called viticulture) is the science and **cultivation of grapes**, especially for the production of wine.
 
• **Sericulture** is the cultivation of silkworms for the **production of silk**.
 
• The most common silkworm used for silk production is the** Bombyx mori (mulberry silkworm)**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of the President shall be completed before the expiration of the term?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 62.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 62 of the Indian Constitution specifically mentions that an** election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office **of the President must be completed before the expiration of the term.
 
• This ensures a seamless transition of presidential powers without a vacancy in the office.
 
• The election process is governed** to maintain continuity **in the functioning of the highest office in the country.
 
• The article also covers **provisions related to vacancies** due to other causes such as death or resignation.
 
• Timely elections are mandated to avoid any constitutional crisis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 59:**

 
 
• Article 59 lays down the **qualifications and conditions **of the office of the President.
 
• It states that the President should not hold any other office of profit and reside in the official residence during the term.
 
• The President is entitled to specific privileges, including salary and emoluments, during the tenure.
 
 
 
• **Article 61:**
 
 
• Article 61 deals with the** procedure for the impeachment of the President.**
 
• It outlines the process to remove the President from office for violation of the Constitution.
 
• The impeachment process requires a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Article 60:**
 
 
• Article 60 specifies the** oath of office for the President of India.**
 
• The President swears to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of India and ensure the law is faithfully upheld.
 
• This article pertains to the responsibilities assumed by the President upon taking office.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: In which of the following animals are the stinging capsules located around the mouth and on the tentacles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adamsia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Adamsia,** also known as the sea anemone**, is a marine animal that possesses **stinging capsules called nematocysts,** located around the mouth and on the tentacles.
 
• These nematocysts help in capturing prey by delivering a venomous sting that immobilizes small organisms.
 
• Adamsia is a cnidarian and is** known for its symbiotic relationship with hermit crabs.**
 
• The tentacles of Adamsia are highly specialized for defense and feeding.
 
• These stinging cells are characteristic of members of the **phylum Cnidaria**.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f4ad8f551a28d3cf203b787faf7b7a9697eb060dc68b5837b0670317a34e11.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Taenia:**

 
 
• Taenia is a **parasitic flatworm (tapeworm) **that resides in the intestines of vertebrates.
 
• It lacks specialized structures like stinging capsules or tentacles.
 
• It uses hooks and suckers on its scolex (head) to attach to the host's intestine.
 
• Taenia is primarily known for causing diseases like taeniasis in humans.
 
 
 
• **Nereis:**
 
 
• Nereis is a** polychaete worm belonging to the phylum Annelida.**
 
• It has parapodia for locomotion but does not possess stinging capsules or tentacles.
 
• Nereis is a marine organism often found in burrows or swimming in water.
 
• Its feeding strategy involves using a proboscis rather than stinging mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Ascaris:**
 
 
• Ascaris is a** parasitic roundworm found in the intestines of humans and other animals.**
 
• It does not have stinging capsules or tentacles; instead, it survives by absorbing nutrients from the host's intestines.
 
• Ascaris causes ascariasis, a parasitic infection, but lacks any external structures like nematocysts for defense or hunting.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara empire included people from different cultural regions. Which of the following regions was NOT a part of it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maratha.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Maratha region was not part of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The empire mainly encompassed regions of **southern India, while the Maratha region is in western India** (modern-day Maharashtra).
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire primarily controlled regions to the south of the Maratha lands during its height.
 
• The Maratha region gained prominence later under the Maratha Empire, which** rose after the decline of the Vijayanagara Empire in the 17th century.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tamil:**

 
 
• The Tamil region was a** significant part **of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The empire** included Tamil-speaking areas**, particularly in present-day Tamil Nadu.
 
• Vijayanagara rulers had close ties with Tamil dynasties and controlled important Tamil centers like Madurai.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka:**
 
 
• Karnataka was the** core region** of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• The empire was founded in this region,** with Hampi (in present-day Karnataka) as its capital.**
 
• Many of the Vijayanagara rulers were of Kannada-speaking origin.
 
 
 
• **Telugu:**
 
 
• The Telugu region (modern-day Andhra Pradesh) was a **crucial part **of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• Telugu warriors and nobles played significant roles in the administration and military.
 
• The empire's founders also had **Telugu roots, and Telugu culture flourished** under their rule.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Vijayanagara Empire was **founded in 1336 by the brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I.** 
 
• The empire was named after its capital city, Vijayanagara, which is now the ruined city of** Hampi in Karnataka**, India. 
 
• The empire was predominantly** Hindu but also accepted other faiths such as Jainism and Islam.** 
 
• The empire was known for its art and culture, including architecture, literature, and religious tolerance. 
 
• The empire reached its peak in the early 16th century under the rule of** Krishnadevaraya, who wrote the epic poem Amuktamalyada.** 
 
• The empire's power declined after the** Battle of Talikota in 1565** when the combined armies of the Deccan sultanates defeated the Vijayanagara army and destroyed the capital city. The empire fell in 1646. 
 
• The ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site. **
 
• The largest festival in the Vijayanagara Empire was** Mahanavami, also known as Navaratri or Dussehra.**

questions.question: The Great Bath was found in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjo-Daro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most famous building to be found in the Harappan excavation was the **Great Bath at** **Mohenjodaro**.
 
• Mohenjodaro is the second most important town of the **Harappan civilization**.
 
• It is located in the Larkana district in Sind (present-day Pakistan).
 
• The word **Mohenjodaro** means the **mound of the dead**.
 
• **Great Bath** is 12m long, 7m wide and 3m deep. 
 
 
• There were side rooms for changing clothes.
 
• It is believed that the Great Bath served some sort of ritual bathing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ropar (Rupnagar)**

 
 
• Ropar is one of the oldest archaeological sites in India, associated with the **Indus Valley Civilization** (**IVC**). Excavations have revealed artifacts that indicate a thriving urban settlement.
 
• It is located in **Punjab**, Ropar is situated on the banks of the **Sutlej River**, which played a crucial role in the region's agriculture and trade.
 
 
 
• **Alamgirpur**
 
 
• Alamgirpur is another site linked to the** Indus Valley Civilization**, located in Uttar Pradesh. Excavations have uncovered evidence of advanced urban planning, including drainage systems and kiln-fired bricks.
 
• Artifacts found at **Alamgirpur** provide insights into the daily life, trade, and culture of the people during the IVC era, indicating a significant level of social organization.
 
 
 
• **Rakhigarhi**
 
 
• **Rakhigarhi** is one of the **largest sites** of the **Indus Valley Civilization**, located in Haryana. It spans over **350** **hectares **and is considered a key site for understanding the IVC's urban structure and layout.
 
• Ongoing excavations have revealed well-planned streets, residential areas, and evidence of agriculture, highlighting the region's importance in ancient trade networks and its advanced **societal structure**.

questions.question: Sanskrit College at Benaras was founded by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jonathan Duncan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sanskrit College** at **Benaras **was founded in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan, the then** British Resident of Banaras**, to promote the study of Hindu scriptures and classical Indian literature.
 
• The Sanskrit College was established to promote the **study of Sanskrit and classical Indian literature**, serving as a center for learning and education in traditional Indian texts.
 
• The college played a significant role in reviving interest in Sanskrit studies and contributed to the broader **educational reforms during the British colonial** **period** in India.
 
• The college played a crucial role in the **19th-century Indian renaissance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **William Jones:**

 
 
• An English philologist and scholar who founded the **Asiatic Society of Bengal **in** 1784**, which promoted the study of Asian languages, literature, and culture.
 
• He is known for his work in comparative linguistics and for introducing the term "Indo-European" to describe a language family.
 
 
 
• **James Mill:**
 
 
• A Scottish historian and philosopher known for his work "The History of British India," published in **1817**. He argued for utilitarian reforms in India.
 
• Mill was a **strong proponent of education.**
 
 
 
• **Thomas Munro:**
 
 
• A British administrator in India known for his work in the** administrative and revenue systems** in South India.
 
• He was involved in **educational reforms**.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers is considered as the greatest king of Satavahana dynasty and is described as the destroyer of the Sakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Gautamiputra Satakarni__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gautamiputra Satakarni** was a ruler of the **Satavahana** dynasty. **Gautamiputra **means “son of Gautami”.
 
• He had the titles of **Eka Brahamana**, **Trisamudradisvara** and **Agamanilaya**.
 
• Satvahana King Gautamiputra Satakarni bears the Mother’s name.
 
• He was the first Satvahana king to do so.
 
• The source of information about Gautamiputra Satakarni is his coins, the Satavahana inscriptions, and the royal genealogies in the various Puranas.
 
• His mother's name was **Gautami Balashri**.
 
• Her **Nasik Prasasti **gives elaborated information about Gautamiputra Satakarni.
 
• Gautamiputra revived the Satavahana power after a decline caused by **Saka **invasions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simuka **established the Satavahana Dynasty.
 
• They were the primary **local **Indian rulers to issue their coins with the representations of the rulers.
 
• This was begun by Gautamiputra Satakarni who determined the hone from the **Western** **Satraps **after vanquishing them.
 
• Simuka is specified as the primary lord in a list of royals in a Satavahana** inscription at Naneghat**.
 
• The different Puranas state that the primary ruler of the line specifies his title differently as Sishuka, Sindhuka, Chhismaka, Shipraka, etc.
 
• The star of the Satavahana run the show is dated variously from **271 BCE** to **30 BCE**. 
 
• Concurring to the Puranas, the primary Andhra lord toppled the Kanva run the show. He is named **Balipuccha** in a few writings.

questions.question: As of July 2023, who is the Chief Minister of Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himanta Biswa Sarma**__**. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Himanta Biswa Sarma has been serving as the **Chief Minister of Assam since May 10, 2021.**
 
• He is a senior leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and played a crucial role in strengthening the party's presence in Assam and the Northeastern states.
 
• Before becoming the Chief Minister, Sarma held several important portfolios in the Assam government, including Health, Finance, Education, and PWD.
 
• Himanta Biswa Sarma holds a** law degree from Government Law College, Guwahati,** and a PhD from Gauhati University.
 
• As CM, he has focused on infrastructure development, law enforcement reforms, and anti-drug campaigns in the state, along with initiatives for social welfare and education reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MK Stalin**

 
 
• M.K. Stalin has been the **Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu** since May 2021.
 
• He is the President of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam **(DMK**) and son of former CM M. Karunanidhi.
 
• Stalin's government focuses on welfare schemes like financial aid for women and improvements in health, education, and industrial sectors.
 
• Before becoming CM, he served as the** Minister for Rural Development** and held various leadership roles, including Deputy Chief Minister.
 
 
 
• **Arvind Kejriwal**
 
 
• Arvind Kejriwal has been serving as the **Chief Minister of Delhi since February 2015.**
 
• He is the national convener of the Aam Aadmi Party **(AAP), which was founded in 2012.**
 
• Kejriwal's government focuses on education, healthcare (Mohalla Clinics), and free electricity/water schemes.
 
• He is a former** Indian Revenue Service (IRS)** officer and gained prominence through the India Against Corruption movement led by Anna Hazare.
 
 
 
• **Hemant Soren**
 
 
• Hemant Soren has been serving as the **Chief Minister of Jharkhand** since December 2019.
 
• He is the** leader of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM),** a regional political party in Jharkhand.
 
• Soren's government focuses on tribal welfare, land rights, and schemes like "Sona Sobran Dhoti Saree" and employment generation.
 
• Hemant Soren is the son of Shibu Soren, a prominent tribal leader and former Chief Minister of Jharkhand.

questions.question: Under which account heading has the funding for the Kashi Yatra Scheme been approved in India for the year 2022-23?

options.text: Assistance to Char Dham Yatra pilgrims

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Assistance to Manasa Sarovara pilgrims**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The funding for the Kashi Yatra Scheme has been approved under the account heading “Assistance to Manasa Sarovara Pilgrims”.
 
• The approval for this scheme was given for the financial year 2022-23.
 
• The scheme provides financial assistance to pilgrims who wish to undertake the Kashi Yatra, a spiritual journey to Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Pilgrims are eligible to receive financial aid of ₹5,000 under this scheme.
 
• This initiative is the Karnataka state government's effort to support religious tourism for its residents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra Yojana (Delhi)**

 
 
• This scheme offers senior citizens free pilgrimage tours to various religious destinations such as Varanasi, Rameswaram, Shirdi, and others, organized by the Delhi government.
 
 
 
• **Baristha Nagarika Tirtha Yatra Yojana (Odisha)** 
 
 
• Offers subsidized pilgrimage tours for senior citizens to holy sites like Puri, Varanasi, Haridwar, and others, organized by the Odisha government.
 
 
 
• **Prasadam Scheme (Central Government)**
 
 
• This scheme is aimed at the development of pilgrimage sites and heritage destinations across India, focusing on improving infrastructure and services for pilgrims.
 
 
 
• **Teerth Darshan Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)**
 
 
• Provides financial assistance for senior citizens from Madhya Pradesh to undertake pilgrimage tours to sacred sites like Dwarka, Amarnath, Jagannath Puri, and others.

questions.question: ______ is the proper management of a natural resource to prevent its exploitation, destruction or degradation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Conservation**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Conservation refers to the **proper management and use of natural resources** to prevent their exploitation, destruction, or degradation.
 
• The primary aim of conservation is to ensure the sustainable use of natural resources for future generations.
 
• Conservation efforts can be divided into **two main categories.** 
 
• **In-situ conservation** (protecting species in their natural habitats) and ex-situ conservation
